I agree it's not ideal. Some options


1. `gen_ai.agent.id` - Since https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/242, it's clear that `gen_ai.agent.id` is static and 1:1 with a process and only needs to be on resource.
   - For internal invoke agent spans, we can deprecate it.
   - For remote invoke agent client spans, we can add "peer" to all of these attributes to disambiguate (https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/243#issuecomment-4619229448) -> `gen_ai.agent.peer.id`. That's in line with `service.peer.*` (https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/pull/3097).
1. `gen_ai.agent.name` - This is already widely adopted for naming subagents in the same process.
   - Option 1, rename the telemetry level attribute to indicate that it identifies the local subagent -> `gen_ai.subagent.name`. (this is my preference if we had no tech debt)
   - Option 2, since that would break lots of existing usage of this attribute, rename the entity/resource attribute in this PR with "root" or something similar -> `gen_ai.root_agent.name`

subagents can be internal and won't know if they are subagents or main ones

Ideally it could work like this (in the future once/if https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/oteps/entities/4665-multiple-resource-in-sdk.md is implemented): 

```
- invoke_agent (main agent entity)
  - llm stuff
  - agent-as-tool 
    - invoke_agent (sub agent entity) # if not entity, we still need to record it, option 1 breaks here
      - llm stuff
      - agent-as-tool 
         - invoke_agent (sub-sub agent entity) # Option 2.1 breaks here
```

In this case nobody uses resource attributes or agent.name on span / metric attributes. Each agent object instance has it's own tracer/meter with specific to this agent entity.

----------------

I see 3 options:

1. don't even introduce entity until we can support different entities for in-process agents. agent attributes always go on signals. 
2. Option 2.2 - main / root agent entity. Main/root agent spans and metrics will have the same info in resource  attrs and signal attrs.
    - Not sure if it'll be useful if/when multi-entity support will happen.
3. Current shape of this PR (same attributes on resource and signals) and tolerate the pain until multiple entities are supported

---

to this point:

> which might(?) cause issues in Prometheus and other backends

Prometheus should be fine - it [doesn't (at least yet) understand](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/efceef79720efc238645666139a7cee1b0145df1/specification/compatibility/prometheus_and_openmetrics.md#resource-attributes-1) resource attributes.

another thought: we can't even assign entity to in-process subagents now - `gen_ai.agent.id` does not make sense for them. 

Maybe we should have `agent` entity (name+version) and `hosted_agent` (the one with id)  entities? This aligns with option 2.2.

> subagents can be internal and won't know if they are subagents or main ones

Agreed, the application author/framework has to choose one to put in the resource attributes.

> Maybe we should have `agent` entity (name+version) and `hosted_agent` (the one with id) entities?

Why would hosted agent not have a name?
sorry, I meant that only hosted agent would have an id (plus name and version), sub-/local agents would not have static id

1. No entity at all

## Reference evaluation

> Evaluated with the proposed [`reference` skill](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/377) against the authoritative PR diff.

### Findings

1. **Blocking — A2A cannot provide the required entity identity.**  
   [`gen_ai.main_agent.id`](https://github.com/aabmass/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/a009bee720bcb03d50c7c808eab34626681bbb7c/reference/scenarios/a2a/scenario.py#L132-L138) is a fabricated URN. A2A `AgentCard` exposes `name` and `description`, but no stable identifier. Because the model requires `id` and prohibits transient or generated identifiers, this scenario must not claim `gen_ai.main_agent` coverage.

2. **Blocking — no credible reference remains for the new entity associations.**  
   The model associates `gen_ai.main_agent` with internal invoke-agent, execute-tool, workflow, and plan spans, but A2A is the only updated scenario and cannot emit the required identity. Add coverage from a supporting library with a stable identifier or record the associations as honest capture gaps.

3. **High — A2A falsely claims execute-tool support.**  
   The [`execute_tool` span](https://github.com/aabmass/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/a009bee720bcb03d50c7c808eab34626681bbb7c/reference/scenarios/a2a/scenario.py#L47-L56) wraps only `pass`; every tool attribute is synthetic. Remove this coverage or invoke a real tool boundary.

4. **High — invoke-agent attributes are not captured from the operation.**  
   [`conversation.id`, input, and output](https://github.com/aabmass/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/a009bee720bcb03d50c7c808eab34626681bbb7c/reference/scenarios/a2a/scenario.py#L35-L70) are hardcoded despite direct sources in `context.context_id`, `context.message`, and the emitted `Message`. The span also closes before `enqueue_event`, so it does not wrap the complete operation.

5. **Medium — the claimed client span is internal.**  
   [`start_as_current_span`](https://github.com/aabmass/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/a009bee720bcb03d50c7c808eab34626681bbb7c/reference/scenarios/a2a/scenario.py#L108-L126) omits `kind=SpanKind.CLIENT`, so the report classifies it as `invoke_agent_internal`.

### Convention changes

- Add the `gen_ai.main_agent` entity.
- Require `gen_ai.main_agent.id`; recommend `name` and `description`.
- Associate the entity with internal invoke-agent, execute-tool, workflow, and plan spans.
- Change relevant `gen_ai.agent.name` requirement levels.

### Field classification

| Field | Classification | Current-call source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gen_ai.main_agent.id` | capture gap | A2A `AgentCard` has no stable ID; the URN is test scaffolding |
| `gen_ai.main_agent.name` | direct, implementation needs fixing | `card.name` |
| `gen_ai.main_agent.description` | direct, implementation needs fixing | `card.description` |

### Libraries not updated

| Library | Evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| `aws-bedrock-agent` | `gen_ai.main_agent.id` is direct from the stable `agentId` invocation argument; add reference coverage, noting that the current scenario emits client spans rather than the new internal associations |
| `agent-framework` | weak; its scenario uses an application-supplied `"weather-agent"` ID with no demonstrated stability |
| `azure-ai-foundry`, `openai-assistants` | honest capture gap in the current scenarios; provider IDs are returned only after ephemeral agent creation, after the OTel resource is initialized |
| `autogen`, `crewai`, `google-adk`, `openai-agents`, `pydantic-ai`, `langchain` | honest capture gap; current examples expose names or process-local objects but no stable main-agent identity |

### Capture gaps

- **A2A:** needs a stable identifier exposed by the Agent Card or server configuration; none is available.
- **Internal framework spans:** need a stable, non-process-local main-agent identifier available when the OTel resource is created.
- **Provider-created agents:** need an existing persistent agent identity available before telemetry-provider initialization.

### Validation

Reviewed the current `gh pr diff`, the A2A SDK `AgentCard` and `RequestContext` surfaces, and existing agent/workflow/plan scenarios. No test suite was run. The PR currently conflicts with `main`.
